reason: Staged first-party GA4 loader previously accepted Cookie Notice setCookieNotice('true') when the notice cookie was true; a synthetic CustomEvent plus cookie write could enable a fresh versioned consent marker without a user clicking Accept.

installed_plugin_evidence.observed_behavior: Cookie Notice attaches click listeners to .cn-set-cookie links; handler calls setStatus(this.dataset.cookieSet); setStatus writes cookie_notice_accepted=true or false first and immediately dispatches synthetic CustomEvent('setCookieNotice', { detail: {value, time, expires, data:cnArgs} }).
installed_plugin_evidence.consequence: The custom setCookieNotice event is not a trusted browser event; gating on event.isTrusted would wrongly block legitimate user consent.

mitigation.name: Trusted click intent verification and consume-once
mitigation.mechanism: Capture a browser-trusted click (event.isTrusted===true) on exact #cn-accept-cookie before Cookie Notice's synchronous setStatus/event dispatch. On setCookieNotice('true') require a new trusted-intent timestamp no older than 1500ms and cookie_notice_accepted=true. Consume the click intent before marking accepted, even on validation failure. Reject still fails closed without proof-of-click requirement.
mitigation.limitation: A same-origin malicious script with full page execution can still manipulate cookies, event handlers or Google tags; this is defense-in-depth against accidental programmatic acceptance and not cryptographic attestation of the visitor's will.
mitigation.keyboard: Enter/Space activating the browser's accessible Accept link produces a trusted click event and follows the same path; actual assistive technology/browser behavior remains untested.
mitigation.scope: Only the separately approved GA4 adapter in the approved site; no public Cookie Notice plugin or WordPress changes.
